chain.label: Execuflight's casual attitude toward compliance; no SMS, FDM, or effective operational oversight
chain.trigger: Execuflight's casual attitude towards compliance with standards illustrates a disregard for operational safety, an attitude that likely led its pilots to believe that strict adherence to SOPs was not required

chain.label: FAA's insufficient surveillance of Execuflight's training and flight operations
chain.trigger: the FAA failed to provide adequate oversight of Execuflight's pilot training, maintenance, and operations; the POI 'did not conduct en route checks with Execuflight or any of his other Part 135 operators'

chain.label: IMC at AKR with the ceiling essentially at the MDA
chain.trigger: 1438 automated weather at AKR was reporting an overcast ceiling of 600 ft agl, a visibility of 1 1/2 mi in mist; the preceding airplane 'broke out right at minimums'

chain.label: First officer hired despite documented inability to fly to standards; crew's CRM and nonprecision-approach training ineffective
chain.trigger: the first officer's performance remained 'significantly below acceptable standards'... deficiencies in Execuflight's CRM training program... resulted in the flight crew receiving inadequate CRM training

caused_by.evidence: because Execuflight did not fully evaluate the information it had concerning the first officer's significant training difficulties at his previous employer, the company missed an opportunity to determine if the first officer was fully capable of operating its airplanes safely
The FAA's oversight system did not identify or address the deficiencies in Execuflight's training that were discovered during this investigation

chain.label: First officer likely fatigued from circadian disruption and inadequate rest before the trip
chain.trigger: as a result of circadian disruption and Execuflight's improper crew scheduling that did not provide the first officer with adequate rest for his preceding trip, the first officer was likely experiencing fatigue

caused_by.evidence: neither the chief pilot nor Execuflight's president ensured that the first officer met the rest requirements of 14 CFR 135.267(d) before assigning him to fly the overnight trip

chain.label: Captain let the weaker first officer fly the nonprecision approach to near-minimums in IMC
chain.trigger: Contrary to Execuflight's informal practice of the captain acting as pilot flying on flights carrying revenue passengers, the first officer was the pilot flying, and the captain was the pilot monitoring

caused_by.evidence: the chief pilot said it was the 'captain's discretion' to decide if the first officer was competent to fly an instrument approach
no evidence that Execuflight evaluated the first officer's abilities despite his recent and extensive documented training difficulties

chain.label: Captain (PM) briefed the approach instead of the PF; briefing incomplete and Approach checklist never accomplished
chain.trigger: the first officer said, 'I'll let you brief it to me'... The ensuing approach briefing was unstructured, inconsistent, and incomplete, and the approach checklist was not completed

caused_by.evidence: Execuflight had established SOPs, but the flight crew consistently failed to follow them
the first officer, as the pilot flying, was required by the GOM to brief the pilot monitoring

chain.label: No shared understanding of the approach; captain coached rather than commanded and omitted required callouts
chain.trigger: the captain and first officer did not have a shared understanding of how the approach was to be conducted... the captain inappropriately adopted the duties of a flight instructor and did so ineffectively

caused_by.evidence: as a result of the flight crew's failure to complete the approach briefing and the Approach checklist as per SOPs, the captain and first officer did not have a shared understanding
the flight crew did not demonstrate effective CRM during the accident flight

chain.label: Crew lost awareness of aircraft state: no descent to 2,300 ft after clearance, and decaying airspeed unnoticed by the first officer
chain.trigger: the first officer did not initiate a descent, the captain failed to notice, and the airplane remained level at 3,000 ft msl... 'no. one tw--. how do you get one twenty?'

caused_by.evidence: It was apparent that the first officer had lost situational awareness of the approach, and the circumstances were demanding more than his capabilities
The first officer exhibited some behaviors consistent with fatigue, such as fixation and degradation of visual scan, difficulty reasoning
the first officer was having difficulty flying the airplane in IMC

chain.label: First officer slowed to about 125 knots with 12 degrees nose-up pitch, far below the 144-knot flaps-25 approach speed
chain.trigger: the pitch of the airplane increased from about 5° to 12° nose up, and the airspeed slowed from about 150 to 125 knots... 'because we gonna stall. I don't want to sta--'

caused_by.evidence: The first officer's speed reduction placed the airplane in danger of an aerodynamic stall if the speed continued to decay, but the first officer apparently did not realize it
he was not sufficiently familiar with the nonprecision approach procedures on the Hawker 700A to execute the approach safely

chain.label: First officer selected flaps 45 before the FAF, contrary to the Hawker 700A nonprecision profile; captain did not question it
chain.trigger: the first officer requested 45° flaps... contrary to Execuflight's Hawker 700A nonprecision approach profile, which required the airplane to be flown at flaps 25° until after descending to the MDA and landing was assured

caused_by.evidence: the captain did not question the first officer's decision to conduct the approach with flaps 45° and failed to make the required flap callouts
It was also contrary to the training both pilots received on nonprecision approaches at CAE Simuflite

chain.label: Crossed the FAF 400 ft high, then dove at 2,000 fpm to salvage the approach
chain.trigger: the airplane crossed the FAF at an altitude of about 2,700 ft msl... The airplane's rate of descent quickly increased to 2,000 fpm, likely due to the first officer attempting to salvage the approach

caused_by.evidence: Because the airplane was high on the approach, it was out of position to use a normal descent rate of 1,000 fpm to the MDA
exacerbated by the increased drag resulting from the improper flaps 45° configuration

chain.label: Approach was unstabilized at the MDA (113 knots, flaps 45) but the mandated missed approach was not flown
chain.trigger: when the airplane reached the MDA, the approach was not stabilized, and the captain should have called for a missed approach according to SOPs, but he did not do so

caused_by.evidence: the descent rate had decreased to about 830 fpm, the airspeed was too slow at 113 knots
the airplane was improperly configured with full flaps
the airspeed was 11 knots below the minimum required airspeed of 124 knots

chain.label: Captain directed continued descent below the MDA without the runway environment in sight
chain.trigger: at 1452:20.5, he said, 'keep going,' although he made no reference to visually acquiring the PAPI or runway environment as required by 14 CFR 91.175(c)(1) for descent below the MDA

caused_by.evidence: Rather than calling for a missed approach... the first officer complied with it and continued the descent
a descent below minimum descent altitude without visual contact with the runway environment

chain.label: At the level-off call, thrust and pitch were not managed to counter the flaps-45 drag
chain.trigger: the first officer did not appropriately manage pitch and thrust control inputs to counter the increased drag from the 45° flap setting

caused_by.evidence: at 1452:27.3, about 14 seconds after the airplane descended below the MDA, the captain said 'okay level off guy'

Maintaining altitude and airspeed at flaps 45° required a fuel flow of about 1,150 lbs per hour per engine, significantly more than the 800 lbs per hour per engine that Execuflight pilots were trained to apply

chain.label: Aerodynamic stall at about 98 knots with AOA exceeding the 15.5-degree critical value
chain.trigger: the airplane was likely in a stalled condition as indicated by an estimated airspeed of 98 knots and an estimated AOA of 21°, which exceeded the critical AOA of 15.5°; the stick shaker activated

caused_by.evidence: the airplane entered a stalled condition when the first officer attempted to arrest the descent
because the flight crew had lost awareness of airspeed and allowed the airspeed to decay below VREF, there was little margin for error
As a result of the increased drag due to the improper flaps 45° configuration and the low airspeed

chain.label: Departed controlled flight in a left-wing-down attitude about 1.8 nm from the runway
chain.trigger: the airplane departed controlled flight while on a nonprecision localizer approach; a security camera captured the airplane in a left-wing-down attitude

caused_by.evidence: the captain's mismanagement of the approach placed the airplane in an unsafe situation that ultimately resulted in the loss of control

chain.label: Struck trees and power lines and impacted a four-unit apartment building; destroyed by impact and postcrash fire
chain.trigger: the airplane struck tree branches and power lines before impacting terrain in the front yard of a four-unit apartment building... An explosion and postcrash fire were observed

caused_by.evidence: About 7 seconds after the captain's instruction to level off, the cockpit voice recorder recorded the first sounds of impact

chain.label: Captain, first officer, and seven passengers died; escape precluded by the postcrash fire
chain.trigger: The captain, first officer, and seven passengers died; no one on the ground was injured... the impact forces were survivable for some occupants, but the immediate and rapidly spreading postcrash fire likely precluded the possibility of escape

caused_by.evidence: the cause of death for both pilots was 'inhalation of products of combustion and thermal injury'; five passengers died of blunt force trauma
